title: When do you think people will be excited about games developed with AI?
author: pianokayak
selftext:
I'm talking specifically about Steam and maybe even other consoles, but ultimately, people have been using all kinds of new tools forever. There's always been some sort of backlash, at least temporarily, when new tools are introduced that potentially change the way that people see things or the way that things are being developed.

My question is: at what point will people say, "Okay, this is cool"? Is it just that no one's come out with a great game yet? Is that really what it is, or is it different than that? Is it more people standing on principle, because eventually everybody is going to be using AI? Everybody is using AI right now already. That's the reality. Everybody's been using AI, autocomplete, and all kinds of things up to now. At what point will you be able to say on Steam, "Hey, this is an AI-assisted game, and people are okay with it"?

comments.author: SimCFB
comments.body:
When they are good. 

I think what a lot of these Indy game developers will find. Is what I found. That if you want to make a good game you still have to sink a ton of time into it. The coding time requirement has collapsed a bit. But there's still a ton to figure out if you actually want a good product.

But yeah when people start making fun AI games. Everyone will stop giving a shit.

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body:
I really want that to be true. If that's the case, then I'm excited. I've been spending hundreds of hours on a game so far, and I easily have probably somewhere between 500 and 700 more hours before I finish this game, but it is freaking amazing.

I've worked on it with my kids and gotten their feedback, and they've helped me design things and make decisions. We've worked through this. I'm using AI, Codex, and Fable, and I'm using all kinds of other tools besides that, but AI is enabling me to build a game that is actually really awesome. If the game really is actually awesome, maybe people will be okay with that. That's what I want to see.

replies.author: keaslenyt
replies.body:
Well it's still a bit of a hit and miss with the AntiAI crowd, I'm afraid.  
I've had some mixed results with the game I made. I think it came out really well. It is obvious that I used AI for art (and I don't try to hide that fact) and whenever I post anything on reddit, there are always those who comment along the lines of "AI Slop" and "I would never spend money on a game that was made with AI" and such.   
  
It's super frustrating when you spent a lot of time and tons of effort to make something that is actually a complete and working game that looks decent and plays well, and then have people react that way (without even giving it an honest try)... But, one thing that I can tell you is - don't listen to them, don't worry about them, and carry on doing what you do. I realised in the last few weeks that in a way we are already there - if your game is good then it will be accepted and welcomed. It turns out that while they are very vocal and feel it is their duty to put you down, there are actually not that many of them. I found that for every useless regurgitated "It's AI Slop!" kind of comment, I still get 5-10 wishlists on Steam. So, don't pay attention to them and carry on.   
  
If you and your kids like the game, then it is likely that other dads and kids will like the game.  
It's still early in the technology lifecycle, so there is still a lot of resistance, and considering the nature of AI and it's power, I expect that it will last for a while yet... But that shouldn't stop you.   
Also, there are some AI friendly subs, so stick to those in the early stages - you can get some good feedback and advice there before you throw it to the wolves ;)

Good luck and keep on doing it!

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body: Agreed that it’s good to start with the friendly subs. This one is good. Any others you recommend? Also, what’s your game??

comments.author: Snoo-29395

replies.author: Destituted
replies.body:
I think that’s the answer to the question!  So if Unreal Engine just came out and suddenly a ton of games were being put on Steam within a few months all clearly using the Unreal Engine templates and stock assets (the white cyborg model they give you) people would be sick of Unreal Engine.

Then over time, developers have poured more time into their games where it’s no longer obvious where this game came from, it’s just well polished and designed.

AI has been good enough for really good games probably for about 6 months now and into next year we will start seeing more and more games coming out where the AI is not apparent.

What I think will happen is AI will continue to get better at everything to the point where developers who use it will refuse to wear Steam’s scarlet letter (AI disclosure), the antis will quiet down because there’s so many and so many they can no longer prove (in their minds lol) and then Steam will eventually remove the disclosure requirement as more lines get blurred with DLSS5.

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body: I totally agree with this, is morally wrong maybe, but if we reach a point where is almost impossible to tell if something is AI generated or not, why would anyone be willing to disclose it?

replies.author: HitMePat
replies.body: The time will come where disclosing it won't matter and won't be required.  Literally everyone will be using it in one shape or form.  The big studios certainly will be.  Games made with zero AI will become like "artisinal organic free range" games, and most people won't care or bother except to maybe comment like "oh wow this was made without any AI? That must have taken forever" as like a novelty.

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body: Yeah, who wants to wait 6 months for an update that could have taken 2 days?

replies.author: pianokayak

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body: Nothing, what can be morally wrong is doing it without disclosing it, as i said on the comment

replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body:
No AAA project going forward will not have some form of Ai usage. Be it code reviews or helper processes at a minimum. Its just going to happen.  As someone who has done a bit of programmer hiring in the last 4 years 80% of submissions have heavy ai usage. in another couple years itll be 95%. 

Which always makes me remember that the rage against Ai isn't for the majority some moral stance its purely a lack of quality. I could point to a ton of new websites that have poped up in the last 3 years that are a vibe coded mess that perform like ass. 

Yet no one really cares because they still do the thing they are meant to do. 

Like you could give someone a multi million dollar team with amazing artists without good direction the output they will produce will be trash still. Ai currently tools outside of programmer are currently a weak team. So the results are just generally poor.

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body: In other words, the outcome is the only thing that really matters. If the game is good, people should be excited about it. And because of AI, small development teams should be able to do updates at lightning fast speed.

replies.author: robhanz
replies.body: Exactly.  Being excited because of the tools used to build a game is a weird t hing.

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body: But people are actively boycotting games that disclose they are using AI. I agree with you. Who cares about the tool? I care about the outcome.

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body:
I agree, but is the same as people boycotting Sony for moving to a digital-only games by 2028, and at the same time increasing the PS5 sales in the last semester. Or people hating Unreal Engine while Expedition 33 won all the awards last year.

What i'm trying to say is that people that complain are the louder, but the smaller group

replies.author: ScutFarkush
replies.body: Dont let the vocal minority ruin for you, focus on making something that is fun, unique, and does not look like ai was involved. I love dev with AI, but I do not like when something looks and feels like ai. Admittedly, this is the hardest part and you cannot just one shot assets, and you may need to composite them through some normal non ai workflows.

replies.author: pyabo
replies.body: Well see, now you get the real question:  When will people stop having knee-jerk reaction to anything created with AI?

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: To be honest I think the current LLMs enable to make quality product to some extent, however the other side is that, it is really hard to tell, which game is actual quality and there is now even more trash quality games then before because you literally can make game from one prompt. I think if someone puts in effort and talent and it can actually compete, it not really matters if the game uses ai or not.

replies.author: Snoo-29395
replies.body:
I think exactly the same, i've been working on a game for 4 months now. Prior to that, i spent 2 years learning and working on courses.

So every time i see "i one shot X game" getting viral, i'm kind of upset not gonna lie. Developing a game takes time, you are only using a tool to help you significantly reduce the time it takes to make it. Have a good idea, good level design, difference what's fun are not, etc. All that takes a lot of practice and iteration, you cannot one shot that, and those viral posts just make the hating snowball bigger

comments.body: AI is already used to some degree in pretty much every game now.

replies.author: pianokayak

replies.author: nsyx
replies.body:
People are mad about it because it competes with them and threatens their livelihoods.

But nobody is questioning the economic system we live in where increases in productivity devalues the economic value of human labor. Karl Marx pointed this 178 years ago and nothing has changed. He called it the Tendency for the Rate of Profit to Fall. The emergence of AI makes this tendency very obvious.

The problem is capitalism, not AI itself. People's anger is misdirected.

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body: AI isn’t competing with my livelihood. It’s expanding my potential. I guess it’s all about how you look at it.

I worked on self-driving cars. In the beginning people were excited about such tech. Then once Elon Musk was involved, people started hating it. They're only there to kill the drivers. comments.author: GilbyScarChest
comments.body: I think the answer to your question is: when the game industry stabilizes to the point where there is a status quo again. What I mean by that is that AI being good enough to create high quality game assets and code game mechanics is very new and absolutely will put people out of work who previously had worked for companies exclusively doing those things, those jobs are going to dry up and those workers will have to expand their skills to stay relevant or work in another field. They’re rightfully pissed about that. However, once the industry finds its new workflow and people are able to see job opportunities for themselves, then they won’t care about AI tools being used. At that point it doesn’t affect them as much and they’ll expect that that’s just how games are made now.

replies.author: pianokayak
replies.body: This is a good answer. During the adjustment phase, people are confused. Once there is more clarity for how the new market works, people will be less up in arms.

replies.author: GilbyScarChest
replies.body: Exactly! Imagine you’ve spent the best years of your life grinding away trying to master Blender, spending thousands of dollars on classes and certifications because all you want to do is build/animate high quality assets for AAA games. And then right as you finally make it a brand new technology comes out that does just as good a job as you but takes seconds and costs almost nothing. If that was me, I would probably want to boycott all AI games too! But soon, kids won’t dream about building assets for games, they’ll just dream of building the whole damn thing and they’ll prepare themselves for a job in gaming that exists in a world where generative AI exists. That’s when nobody will care whether you used AI. They’ll only care that the game looks cool and is fun to play.
